title: Minimal Mask Refreshing for Output Decoding
summary: The full mask-refreshing sequence supports perfect simulation, but the minimum number and placement of refreshes needed for t-th-order security remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: In the output-decoding operation, $n$ output shares are subjected to a series of $n$ mask-refreshing operations before their recombination, and any set of $t$ intermediate variables can be perfectly simulated from at most $2t$ selected shares together with the recombined value. However, the claim that the full series of $n$ refreshings is necessary is only heuristic: determine the minimum number and the required placement of mask-refreshing operations before output-share recombination that are sufficient and necessary to preserve $t$-th-order simulation security, including the dependence on $n$ and $t$.

scope.domain: Higher-order masking and side-channel simulation security for output decoding.
parameters: n: number of output shares and refreshings in the full construction
t: number of intermediate variables considered and target order of simulation security
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine, as a function of n and t, the minimum number and required placement of pre-recombination mask refreshings that are sufficient and necessary for t-th-order simulation security.

citations.label: Higher Order Masking of Look-Up Tables

progress.summary: The source establishes perfect simulation for any t intermediate variables from at most 2t selected shares and the recombined value when the full n-refresh sequence is used. It treats the necessity of all n refreshings only heuristically, leaving their minimum number and placement open.
citation_labels: Jean-Sébastien Coron et al., Higher Order Masking of Look-Up Tables
